items.title: Tolliver interviewed by Monk Rowe, 2021
items.q: I guess my all-time favorite classical composer, musician, is Bartok.

ctx.x: Well you know those fellows, when they were creating that free form thing, and I watched that because I broke in right at the same time, there wasn’t an audience really. There was like a few family and friends. And you know the writers in the magazines gave it a big lift you know. And then people started to say well what is this all about, and started to come. And there were two places on the Lower East Side where this was incubated and really got going. And one was called a speakeasy. Actually that place is…

mean for the beboppers, so-called straight ahead guys, you know some of it got incorporated into, you know, the mainstream of things. And just like with classical music you know, things got worked out. I mean a perfect example is I mean I guess my all-time favorite classical composer, musician, is Bartok. And the reason why is not only is his works, you know, just out of this world great, but you know he said you know I’m really a Bach guy. You know? But he took that and did like what happened with all our form,…

I wondered on occasion if the musicians like yourself and the fellas you mentioned sat around and talked about how they were going to play. Was there discussions that said like we might say, all right, we’re not going to play in this particular time signature, we’re just going to see what happens? Or I guess what I’m trying to say was any of this music pre-planned before you got on the bandstand or did it happen as it was being created?
